summary: A two-player hex-and-card wargame where you build and prune a deck of unit cards over a series of short scenarios, using command cards to activate squads, ambush, and fight for control points. Vehicles, wounded soldiers leaving your deck, and asymmetric British/Italian decks give it a tighter tactical, more mobile feel than the original Normandy entry.
praised: Fast, tense scenarios that teach a real deckbuilding-meets-wargame system without heavy rules overhead
Evolving decks (wounds, reinforcements, vehicles) make each game feel like a narrative battle rather than an abstract exercise
Strong two-player asymmetry between the mobile LRDG raiders and the more static Italian defenders
Solid campaign mode that links scenarios together with persistent consequences
criticised: Dice-based combat resolution introduces swingy luck that can undercut careful positioning
Scenario-to-scenario structure can feel samey if played outside the campaign
Vehicle rules and open desert terrain are seen by some as a step down in tension from Normandy's hedgerow chokepoints
Solo/asymmetric balance across some individual scenarios is uneven

interaction.kind: direct combat and area/objective control on a shared hex map

scoring.why: Each scenario is decided by mission-specific objectives (holding control points, eliminating units, or reaching a zone) rather than an accumulated score
